title: Class-AB output stage (Monticelli)
description: A push-pull class-AB output stage biased the Monticelli way. The NMOS pull-down and PMOS pull-up output devices carry a quiescent current $I_q$ that the class-AB bias branch sets through a translinear loop: the branch's own stacked reference devices fix the sum of the two output devices' gate-source voltages, $V_{GS,n} + |V_{GS,p}|$, and with it the quiescent current, which can then be small (low static power) while the devices still turn fully on under drive. The two gates themselves sit $V_{DD} - (V_{GS,n} + |V_{GS,p}|)$ apart, the voltage the floating control between them holds. The bias branch is not drawn on this sheet, so the two gates are ports; the sheet reports the sum the branch has to produce as vgs_sum and checks nothing against it. Drawn as a child sheet, the branch will derive it. The swing equations give the rail-to-rail output range set by the two saturation voltages. Raising $I_q$ lowers crossover distortion but wastes static power — the class-AB quiescent/efficiency trade. On the demo NMOS table both output devices size against the same data, so the PMOS sign param stays at +1.

params.name: V_out
params.note: quiescent output DC level; sets each output device's vds. The pull-up and pull-down drains meet at a high-impedance output that nothing on this sheet holds; the feedback of the amplifier this stage terminates holds it here

params.name: I_q
params.note: class-AB quiescent current: higher I_q lowers crossover distortion but wastes static power

params.name: gm_id_n
params.note: NMOS output-device inversion (low gm/ID for current drive)

params.name: p_sign
params.note: vds sign of the PMOS device table: +1 for the N-style demo axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

doc.title: NMOS pull-down output device
doc.description: The NMOS output device at the quiescent current; its vds is the output DC level. Its vgs is one half of the translinear-loop sum.

doc.title: PMOS pull-up output device
doc.description: The PMOS output device at the quiescent current; its vds magnitude is the supply minus the output DC. Its vgs is the other half of the translinear-loop sum.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

equations.name: vgs_sum
equations.note: the translinear-loop sum: the gate drive the class-AB bias branch must produce, through its stacked reference devices, to bias both output devices at I_q. Reported, not checked: the branch is not drawn on this sheet, and a typed voltage checked against this sum would only restate what the devices already determine. The branch will come as a child sheet that derives it

equations.name: gm_out
equations.note: push-pull transconductance at quiescent (both devices contribute)

equations.name: swing_hi
equations.note: highest output the PMOS can pull up to while saturated

equations.name: swing_lo
equations.note: lowest output the NMOS can pull down to while saturated

equations.name: swing
equations.note: peak-to-peak output swing between the two saturation limits

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: the resistance this output stage presents at its output — both devices' output conductances in parallel, since at quiescent they conduct together. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this equation is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

checks.note: the rail-to-rail output swing meets the target
